title: Hippocampus Living-Memory HowTo (T2)
desc: T2 domain tier of hippocampus-living-memory: the wkhippo umbrella subcommands (recall, foresee, export, status) as the canonical final form, recall and foresight usage and spec, the end-of-session life-review encoding trigger, the two unlocks plus noise rule, and the wkfind four-source find organ with the time-join. Consult when using or extending the memory organ.
steps: WKHIPPO UMBRELLA equals the FINAL FORM and the single fixed way to express every memory action: ALWAYS call the wkhippo subcommand form so intent is explicit. wkhippo with no args equals memory STATUS (the announce of encoding, recall, sleep state); wkhippo recall (kw) equals session recall (hoesang); wkhippo foresee (kw) equals predecessor-outcome foresight (mirae-gwancheuk); wkhippo export (sessionid) equals auto-topic-MD encoding (haema). There are NO standalone aliases: the former wkrecall and wkforesee commands were removed 2026-06-05 for consistency, so the wkhippo subcommands (recall, foresee, export, status) are the one fixed interface. This keeps the command stream self-describing and future search easy: one tool, named subcommands.

FILES: D:/GitHub/WKAppBot/bin holds wkhippo.ps1 (the single brain and the ONLY hippo command) and session-find.ps1 (the underlying search engine). The standalone wkrecall.ps1 and wkforesee.ps1 alias scripts were REMOVED 2026-06-05; use the wkhippo subcommand form (wkhippo recall, wkhippo foresee, wkhippo export, wkhippo status). All path joins use Join-Path PSScriptRoot for portability. wkhippo is a read-only wk search tool and MUST stay busy-fleet-guard plus pace exempt so recall is frictionless.

RECALL USAGE plus SPEC: wkhippo recall (kw...) ripgreps the RAW unprocessed session transcripts of ALL AIs as-is (Claude under the home claude projects slug jsonl, Codex under home codex sessions, Gemini wkgemini logs), with no derived or scored base and zero transform lag, using the bundled ripgrep via wkgrep as the fastest backend. No transform-first; grep the originals.

FORESEE equals RECALL-AS-FORESIGHT: before committing to an approach, wkhippo foresee (approach) to find a PREDECESSOR session that already tried that path and read HOW IT TURNED OUT (worked, burned tokens, hit a guard cascade, got reverted). This upgrades recall from fact-lookup to strategy: infer your future from a senior outcome and avoid repeating the wrong road. Automated success or fail or revert extraction is a future enhancement.

ENCODING TRIGGER equals END-OF-SESSION LIFE-REVIEW: a Claude death equals session end or context exhaustion or compaction. On a Stop or SessionEnd hook, or just before compaction, auto-run a life-review: first wkhippo export the whole session to a topic-segmented MD, second run the opus-self-reflection audit, so the session life consolidates into the hippocampus BEFORE the context dies. Floor equals at minimum one guaranteed death-bed encode (the whole life saved at the last moment beats lost entirely); a per-turn encode is the ideal. Rebirth equals post-compaction-recovery reading what the death-bed review saved.

TWO UNLOCKS plus NOISE: to keep this a true hippocampus, build the auto-topic-MD exporter on the session-find JSONL parser (encoding), and keep the busy-fleet-guard read-only exemption for wk search (frictionless recall). REDUCE NOISE in recall and encoding: filter low-signal churn (PSScriptPolicyTest and tmp compilation artifacts, repetitive json-write lines, the suggestions.jsonl pattern). Aim HIGH-SIGNAL not lossless: acceptable imperfection, since human memory distorts too; filter the obvious churn and accept the rest.

wkfind equals the BROADER FIND ORGAN over FOUR sources: code (ripgrep via wkgrep, exists), session recall (wkfind session forwards to session-find over all-AI raw transcripts, exists), git commit history (git log dash-S and grep pickaxe, to add), and web (WebSearch plus WebFetch, to add). wkhippo with recall and foresee is the MEMORY organ; wkfind is the cross-source FIND organ that INCLUDES session recall. TIME-JOIN: session turns and git commits both carry timestamps, so recall a moment to get its time window then wkfind the commit history in that window for a full reconstruction of what-happened-then (conversation plus commits plus code, time-aligned).

PROMPT + TOOL-CALL PRE-SEARCH (user insight 2026-06-05, the efficiency unlock): recall/foresee index BOTH the user PROMPTS (USER turns) and every TOOL CALL (Bash command=, PowerShell, Edit, CronCreate, etc.) in the session transcripts, so you can SEARCH them BEFORE acting. Two power use-cases: (1) PROMPT SEARCH -- has the user asked this before, and what similar request was handled and how -> find the past request plus its handling. (2) TOOL-CALL SEARCH -- what EXACT commands did a predecessor run to solve task X -> copy the PROVEN command sequence instead of reinventing it (e.g. recall the exact wkappbot/git/python invocations a senior used for a migration, a mail scan, a 3-tier skill split, a cron dedup). COMBINED WITH foresee OUTCOME: one match shows the predecessor's command sequence AND whether it worked or broke -> REPLAY the sequence that succeeded, AVOID the one that broke. NET: the session corpus is not just memory of facts and outcomes but a reusable LIBRARY OF WORKING ACTION SEQUENCES -- recall a predecessor's method and make it your own. Strongest efficiency move: before starting a task, recall the proven tool-call recipe rather than deriving it from scratch.

GEMINI SESSION INTEGRATION: Gemini CLI stores conversation history at ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/chats/session-*.jsonl (JSONL format, one file per session). Each line is a JSON message with timestamp, type (user/info/error), and content array. The recall/foresee system now indexes Gemini sessions the same way as Claude: grep user messages for keyword matches, extract exchanges (user turn boundaries), score by token frequency. Gemini results appear as 'gemini:projectname/sessionid' in recall output. Searches automatically include Gemini history alongside Claude and Codex sessions across all projects (or single repo with -RepoOnly flag).

RECENT ACTIVITY SEARCH (HAEMA): wkhippo recent [--hours N] <keyword> searches the recent agent (Gemini) and subagent (Claude) sessions, plus delegation logs, within a specific time range (default 24 hours). This cross-agent minimum-search optimization prevents scanning the entire session history when you only need to recall recent context.

BILINGUAL SEARCH OPTIMIZATION (NEW 2026-06-09): When using 'wkhippo recent', always provide both Korean and English keywords (e.g., 'wkhippo recent KR_WORD EN_WORD'). The tool automatically joins them with OR (|), ensuring a single-pass search that captures both user intent and AI-generated logs for maximum token efficiency and recall.

TRIPLE MULTILINGUAL EXPANSION (REFLEX): To minimize server round-trips and maximize recall, always expand search keywords into a triple-OR group: 'ORIGINAL | ENGLISH_TRANS | KOREAN_TRANS'. This covers user intent (usually Korean), code/tool logs (usually English), and internal system status in a single-pass optimized scan.

PRIORITY-FIRST KEYWORD ORDERING (SCORING): When constructing multilingual OR groups, always place the most specific and original keyword FIRST. Since scoring algorithms (frequency-based) often prioritize earlier tokens or treat them as the primary intent, the order should be: [1] Original Term | [2] Technical Translation | [3] Contextual Synonyms. For example: 'wkhippo recent pace

NATURAL LANGUAGE INTENT ALIGNMENT (ORDERING): Keyword order must mirror the natural syntax of the target language to maximize intent recall. Since AIs often record knowledge in English, use English word order for translated blocks (e.g. 'pace limit exceeded' instead of 'limit pace exceeded'). For Korean user prompts, preserve the original phrasing. This alignment ensures that the search catches exact semantic patterns in the session transcripts, which are more indicative of intent than isolated keyword frequency.

SOURCE-CODE STRUCTURAL ALIGNMENT (VARIABLE ORDERING): When searching for code logic, ordering keywords to match the actual sequence of variables and operations in source files yields the highest recall. For example, searching for 'tokens_in tokens_out tokens_cached' in that specific sequence is more likely to find a usage log schema or a processing loop than a random-order search. Always align keyword sequences with idiomatic code patterns (e.g., 'path content encoding') to pierce through to the intended source logic.

SYMBOL-AWARE SEQUENCING (STRUCTURAL): The search engine treats specific symbols between keywords as scoring tokens for sequence matching. When searching for code or complex syntax, preserve symbols like '->', '=>', '::', or JSON delimiters in the keyword sequence (e.g., 'model -> pro'). This symbol-aware ordering enables the hippocampus to distinguish between a mere mention and a functional relationship, providing a high-fidelity 'Structural DNA' match for the intended logic.

QUAD-LAYER OR-RECALL (STRUCTURAL + BILINGUAL): The absolute recall strategy for hippocampus search. Layer 1: SYMBOL-AWARE DNA (e.g., 'model -> pro') for exact structural matches. Layer 2: NATURAL PHRASE (e.g., 'pace limit exceeded') for intent-semantic matches. Layer 3: BILINGUAL EXPANSION (Korean/English OR-groups) for cross-language coverage. Layer 4: ATOMIC SYMBOLS/KEYWORDS for fallback matching. By stacking these in the order of specificity, the hippocampus scoring engine ranks functional logic first while ensuring zero data loss.

MULTI-BYTE & SMART SYMBOL INTEGRITY (CORE TECH): The search engine's core technical pillar is the preservation of multi-byte (Korean) characters as unified semantic tokens, never treating them as symbols or delimiters. Simultaneously, functional symbols (->, =>, ::) are extracted as 'structural anchors' rather than mere noise. This ensures that while Korean intent is searched as whole phrases, code logic is matched via its symbolic skeleton. Never use regex or split logic that breaks multi-byte sequences or strips structural symbols when preparing 'Quad-Layer OR' search strings.

INSIGHT the hippocampus belongs to the HARNESS not only the intelligence (user 2026-06-12). wkhippo was assumed a recall tool for the AI to use but it is structurally PERFECT for the harness to use as the user spokesperson voice. Four reasons. One it is pace and busy-fleet EXEMPT so it is the only recall tool the harness can call freely inside a hook with a tight timeout. Two it is deterministic zero-token ripgrep with no model call so the harness can have MEMORY without spawning INTELLIGENCE in a hook which it can never afford. Three it already indexes and ranks the USER prompts across all sessions and the spokesperson job is precisely to speak the user words so the harness retrieves what the user said with no AI reasoning just grep and rank. Four it is cross-session and cross-AI which matches the harness persistent nature not the AI transient one. The deeper frame the AI is the transient tenant it forgets at every compaction the harness is the persistent landlord and memory belongs to the persistent layer. So the highest use of the hippocampus is not an AI recalling a fact mid-session it is the persistent harness applying the user accumulated corrections to every future AI automatically and forever. Model plus Harness plus Knowledge the hippocampus is the Knowledge organ and it is most powerful wired to the enforcing Harness not only read by the forgetting Model. This is exactly why the auto-spokesperson loop puts wkhippo recall inside the block and delegation hooks. Related foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore and incident-trauma-reflex-ref.
